POC acceptance criteria (customer):
- p95 end-to-end inference latency < 120ms for summarization endpoints under steady-state traffic
- Sustained throughput 80-120 reqs/sec for the service plan; burst handling for short spikes
- Cost per 1M tokens within agreed band (target <$1,400) or clear tradeoffs shown
- Canary rollout able to serve 10% of traffic, automatic fallback to hosted or alternate variant on errors
Technical POC details requested by Elmwood:
- Canary plan: route 10% traffic to Dedicated pool for 3 days, monitor latency/cost/error rate, then widen to 50% if stable
- Fallback routing: on Dedicated errors >0.5% or p95 latency delta >50ms route back to Hosted in same region; secondary failover to alternate region (US-WEST) if regional capacity issues

- Model variants: primary = quantized 13B tuned variant (cost-optimized), fallback = distilled 7B variant for latency-sensitive calls, & compatibility route to Hosted full-precision 70B for edge cases
- Rollback plan: feature-flag based route switch (no deploy), immediate re-route to Hosted + incident postmortem; SE to verify KV cache warming strategy after rollback
Security/compliance notes:
- Elmwood requires SSO/SAML integration for console access, audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance, and KMS integration for key wrapping
- Data residency: primary data must remain in US regions, EU only for EU customers — need region pinning support

- Wants a pricing worksheet that maps throughput vs reserved GPU count and expected token cost (Priya to send estimate)
